title.zh: 卷70 劉藻 傅永 傅竪眼 李神
title.en: Volume 70: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, Li Shen
title.raw: 卷70 劉藻 傅永 傅竪眼 李神 Volume 70: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, Li Shen

sentences.zh: 劉藻 傅永 傅豎眼 李神

translations.literal: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, Li Shen
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, and Li Shen

sentences.zh: 劉藻，字彥先，廣平易陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zao, styled Yansian, was a man of Yiyang in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao, whose courtesy name was Yansian, came from Yiyang in Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖遐，從司馬叡南渡。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Xia followed Sima Rui in crossing south.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Xia had followed Sima Rui when the court crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 父宗之，劉裕廬江太守。

translations.literal: His father Zongzhi was Liu Yu's Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongzhi had served Liu Yu as Administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 藻涉獵羣籍，美談笑，善與人交，飲酒至一石不亂。

translations.literal: Zao broadly perused the classics, excelled at witty talk, was skilled at forming friendships, and could drink up to one dan of wine without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zao read widely in the classics, was a gifted conversationalist, made friends easily, and could drink a full dan of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 永安中，與姊夫李嶷俱來歸國，賜爵易陽子。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era, together with his brother-in-law Li Ni he came to return to the state and was granted the title Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he returned to Wei together with his brother-in-law Li Ni and was ennobled as Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 擢拜南部主書，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed chief clerk of the Southern Department and was known as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief clerk of the Southern Department and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 時北地諸羌數萬家，恃險作亂，前後牧守不能制，姦暴之徒，並無名實，朝廷患之，以藻為北地太守。

translations.literal: At the time several tens of thousands of Qiang households in Beidi, relying on rugged terrain, rose in rebellion; successive governors and prefects could not control them, and violent wrongdoers alike lacked both name and substance. The court was troubled by this and made Zao Administrator of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time tens of thousands of Qiang households in Beidi, sheltered by difficult country, were in revolt. One governor after another had failed to bring them under control, while outlaws of every stripe flourished beyond the reach of law. The court, alarmed by the situation, appointed Zao Administrator of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 藻推誠布信，諸羌咸來歸附。

translations.literal: Zao extended sincerity and spread trust, and all the Qiang came to submit and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zao won them with sincerity and good faith, and the Qiang submitted to him in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 藻書其名籍，收其賦稅，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: Zao registered their names on the rolls, collected their taxes and levies, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled them in the registers, collected their taxes, and won praise at court.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、雍城鎮將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Dragon Chariot and garrison commandant of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of General of the Dragon Chariot and commandant of the Yongcheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 先是氐豪徐成、楊黑等驅逐鎮將，故以藻代之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Di chieftains Xu Cheng, Yang Hei, and others had driven out the garrison commandant, and therefore Zao was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Di chieftains Xu Cheng and Yang Hei had expelled the garrison commandant, and Zao was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，擒獲成、黑等，斬之以徇，羣氐震慴。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison he captured Cheng, Hei, and the rest, beheaded them as a public warning, and all the Di were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the garrison he seized Cheng, Hei, and their followers, executed them as a warning, and the Di were struck with terror.

sentences.zh: 雍州人王叔保等三百人表乞藻為騃奴戍主。

translations.literal: Three hundred men of Yong Province, Wang Shubao and others, submitted a memorial requesting that Zao be made commandant of the Sainu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao petitioned the throne to make Zao commandant of the Sainu garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「選曹已用人，藻有惠政，自宜他敍。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Selection Bureau has already assigned someone; Zao has benevolent administration and should naturally receive another posting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "The Selection Bureau has already filled that post. Zao has governed well and should be given another appointment.

sentences.zh: 」在任八年，遷離城鎮將。

translations.literal: " After eight years in office he was transferred to garrison commandant of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: " After eight years in office he was transferred to commandant of the Licheng garrison.

translations.literal: Note marker [1].
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note [1].

sentences.zh: 太和中，改鎮為岐州，以藻為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the garrison was changed into Qi Province, and Zao was made Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era the garrison was converted into Qi Province, and Zao was appointed its inspector.

sentences.zh: 轉秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 秦人恃嶮，率多粗暴，或拒課輸，或害長吏，自前守宰，率皆依州遙領，不入郡縣。

translations.literal: The people of Qin relied on rugged terrain; for the most part they were violent and rough, some refusing tax payments, some harming senior officials. From earlier times the prefects and magistrates had all governed from the province at a distance and did not enter the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin, sheltered by harsh terrain, were for the most part unruly and violent. Some refused to pay taxes; others killed their superiors. For years the local magistrates had governed from afar through the provincial office and never set foot in the districts themselves.

sentences.zh: 藻開示恩信，誅戮豪橫，羌氐憚之，守宰於是始得居其舊所。

translations.literal: Zao made clear favor and trust, executed and killed the overbearing and violent, and the Qiang and Di feared him; the prefects and magistrates were thereby able at last to reside in their former seats.
translations.idiomatic: Zao governed with mercy and kept his word, while putting down the violent and powerful. The Qiang and Di were cowed, and for the first time the local officials could return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 遇車駕南伐，以藻為東道都督。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went south on campaign, Zao was made commander of the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zao was appointed commander of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 秦人紛擾，詔藻還州，人情乃定。

translations.literal: The people of Qin were in turmoil; an edict ordered Zao back to the province, and popular sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: With Qin in uproar, the court ordered Zao back to his province, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 仍與安南將軍元英征漢中，頻破賊軍，長驅至南鄭，垂平梁州，奉詔還軍，乃不果克。

translations.literal: He then joined General Who Pacifies the South Yuan Ying in campaigning against Hanzhong, repeatedly defeating rebel armies, driving deep to Nanzheng and on the verge of pacifying Liang Province; obeying an edict he returned the army, and thus the conquest was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned in Hanzhong with General Who Pacifies the South Yuan Ying, repeatedly defeating the enemy and driving as far as Nanzheng, where Liang Province lay almost within grasp. Ordered to withdraw, he turned back, and the province was never taken.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南伐，以藻為征虜將軍，督統軍高聰等四軍為東道別將。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south, Zao was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and supervised the four armies of the army supervisors Gao Cong and others as separate commander of the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: On a later southern campaign the emperor made Zao General Who Subdues the Barbarians and placed him in command of four armies under army supervisors such as Gao Cong as deputy commander of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 辭於洛水之南，高祖曰：「與卿石頭相見。

translations.literal: Taking leave south of the Luo River, Emperor Xiaowen said: "I shall meet you at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: As he took his leave south of the Luo River, Emperor Xiaowen said, "I shall see you at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 」藻對曰：「臣雖才非古人，庶亦不留賊虜而遺陛下，輒當釃曲阿之酒以待百官。

translations.literal: " Zao replied: "Although your servant's talent does not match the ancients, I hope I may yet not leave bandit enemies behind for Your Majesty and will straightway pour libation with Qu'a wine to await the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Zao replied, "Though I am no match for the great men of old, I hope at least not to leave the enemy for Your Majesty to deal with. I shall have Qu'a wine ready to welcome the court when you arrive.

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑曰：「今未至曲阿，且以河東數石賜卿。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen laughed greatly and said: "We have not yet reached Qu'a; for now let several dan of Hedong [wine] be granted you.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaowen laughed and said, "We are not at Qu'a yet. Take several dan of Hedong wine for now.

sentences.zh: 」後與高聰等戰敗，俱徙平州。

translations.literal: " Later he was defeated in battle together with Gao Cong and the rest, and all were relocated to Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was defeated along with Gao Cong and the others and was banished to Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 景明初，世宗追錄舊功，以藻為太尉司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Emperor Xuanwu reviewed and recorded his former merit and made Zao Grand Marshal's secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingming era Emperor Xuanwu recognized his past service and appointed him secretary to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 是年六月卒，年六十七，贈錢六萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year he died, aged sixty-seven; six myriad cash was granted for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of that year at the age of sixty-seven. The court granted sixty thousand cash for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 子紹珍，無他才用，善附會，好飲酒。

translations.literal: His son Shaozhen had no other talent or ability, was skilled at ingratiating himself, and loved drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaozhen had little talent beyond a knack for currying favor and a fondness for drink.

sentences.zh: 結託劉騰，騰啟為其國郎中令。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Liu Teng; Teng memorialized and had him made director of the kingdom's palace.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated Liu Teng, who secured his appointment as director of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 襲子爵。

translations.literal: He inherited the son's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's barony.

sentences.zh: 稍遷本州別駕、司空屬，以事免官。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to chief assistant of his native province and to an aide in the Ministry of Works, but because of an affair was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief assistant of his home province and then to an aide in the Ministry of Works, but was dismissed after an official scandal.

sentences.zh: 建義初，詔復，尋除太中大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi an edict restored him; soon after he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era an edict restored him to office, and he was soon made Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，除安西將軍、河北太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was made General Who Pacifies the West and Administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 還朝，久之，拜車騎將軍、左光祿大夫，出為黎陽太守。

translations.literal: Returning to court, after a long interval he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Virtue, then went out as Administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he waited some time before receiving appointment as General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Virtue, then was sent out as Administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 所在無政績。

translations.literal: Wherever he was stationed there was no record of achievement in government.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left no mark of good governance.

sentences.zh: 天平中，坐子尚書郎洪業入於關中，率眾侵擾，伏法。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, because his son Hongye, a secretary in the Masters of Writing, had entered Guanzhong and led a host in raiding and harassing, he suffered the penalty of law.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was executed after his son Hongye, a secretary in the Masters of Writing, fled into Guanzhong and led troops in raids across the border.

sentences.zh: 傅永，字脩期，清河人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yong, styled Xiuqi, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yong, whose courtesy name was Xiuqi, came from Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼隨叔父洪仲與張幸自青州入國，尋復南奔。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his uncle Hongzhong and Zhang Xing in entering the state from Qing Province, but soon fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he followed his uncle Hongzhong and Zhang Xing from Qing Province into Wei territory, but soon fled back south.

sentences.zh: 有氣幹，拳勇過人，能手執鞍橋，倒立馳騁。

translations.literal: He had force of spirit, and in fist fighting and courage surpassed others; he could grasp the saddle arch and ride upside down at full gallop.
translations.idiomatic: He was spirited and fearless, unmatched in brawling and raw courage. He could grip the saddle bow and gallop head-down without falling.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，有友人與之書而不能答，請於洪仲，洪仲深讓之而不為報。

translations.literal: When he was over twenty, a friend wrote him a letter and he could not reply; he asked Hongzhong, and Hongzhong sternly reproved him and would not answer for him.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties a friend wrote to him and he could not compose a reply. He asked Hongzhong to answer for him, but his uncle rebuked him sharply and refused.

sentences.zh: 永乃發憤讀書，涉獵經史，兼有才筆。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon in indignation took up reading books, broadly perused the classics and histories, and also had literary talent and brush.
translations.idiomatic: Stung to shame, Yong threw himself into his books, read widely in the classics and histories, and proved himself a capable writer as well.

sentences.zh: 自東陽禁防為崔道固城局參軍，與道固俱降，入為平齊民。

translations.literal: From the Dongyang prohibition guard he became a garrison-bureau staff officer under Cui Daogu; together with Daogu he surrendered and entered as a pacified Qi commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as a staff officer in the garrison bureau under Cui Daogu at the Dongyang prohibition post. When Daogu surrendered, Yong went with him and was registered among the pacified commoners of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父母並老，飢寒十數年，賴其強於人事，勠力傭丐，得以存立。

translations.literal: Both parents were old; for more than ten years in hunger and cold they relied on his strength in human affairs, striving with hired labor and begging, and thus were able to survive and stand.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were elderly, and for more than a decade the family lived in hunger and cold. Only because Yong was resourceful and worked and begged without rest did they survive.

sentences.zh: 晚乃被召，兼治禮郎，詣長安，拜文明太后父燕宣王廟，[2]賜爵貝丘男，加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Only late was he summoned, concurrently treated as a ceremonial gentleman, went to Chang'an, and performed obeisance at the temple of Empress Dowager Wenming's father, Prince Xuan of Yan; [2] he was granted the title Baron of Beiqiu and given the additional rank General Who Subdues the Waves.
translations.idiomatic: Only later was he summoned to office, first as an acting ceremonial gentleman. He went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of Prince Xuan of Yan, father of Empress Dowager Wenming. [2] He was ennobled as Baron of Beiqiu and promoted to General Who Subdues the Waves.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除中書博士，又改為議郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Erudite of the Palace Secretariat, then changed to Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made an erudite of the Palace Secretariat, then transferred to the post of gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書考功郎中，為大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Merit Review in the Masters of Writing and became Attendant Gentleman of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of merit review in the Masters of Writing, then attendant gentleman to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋轉都督、任城王澄長史，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander and chief administrator to Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, concurrently Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made chief administrator to Prince Cheng of Rencheng and concurrently left assistant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 王肅之為豫州，以永為建武將軍、平南長史。

translations.literal: When Wang Su was in Yuzhou, Yong was made General Who Establishes Might and chief administrator for Pacifying the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su governed Yuzhou, Yong served him as General Who Establishes Might and chief administrator for the southern command.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧慮肅難信，言於高祖。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xi, worried that Su was hard to trust and spoke to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang, uneasy about trusting Su, spoke to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「已選傅脩期為其長史，雖威儀不足，而文武有餘矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "I have already chosen Fu Xiuqi as his chief administrator; although in ceremony and bearing he is insufficient, in civil and military matters he has surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen replied, "I have already appointed Fu Xiuqi as his chief administrator. He may lack polish, but he has more than enough talent for war and statecraft.

sentences.zh: 」肅以永宿士，禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: " Su, because Yong was a long-established subordinate of the court, treated him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " Su treated Yong, a veteran of the Wei court, with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 永亦以肅為高祖眷遇，盡心事之，情義至穆。

translations.literal: Yong also, because Su enjoyed Emperor Xiaowen's favor and gracious treatment, devoted himself utterly in serving him; their bond of feeling and duty was deepest and most harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, knowing that Su enjoyed the emperor's special favor, served him with complete loyalty. Their mutual devotion ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞遣將魯康祚、趙公政眾號一萬，侵豫州之太倉口。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan sent the generals Lu Kangzuo and Zhao Gongzheng with a host proclaimed at ten thousand to invade Taicang Ford in Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan sent his generals Lu Kangzuo and Zhao Gongzheng with a force said to number ten thousand against Taicang Ford in Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 肅令永勒甲士三千擊之。

translations.literal: Su ordered Yong to muster three thousand armored soldiers and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Su ordered Yong to take three thousand armored troops against them.

sentences.zh: 時康祚等軍於淮南，永舍淮北十有餘里。

translations.literal: At the time Kangzuo and the rest were encamped south of the Huai; Yong gave up the north bank of the Huai by more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzuo's army lay south of the Huai while Yong withdrew more than ten li north of the river.

sentences.zh: 永量吳楚之兵，好以斫營為事，即夜分兵二部，出於營外。

translations.literal: Yong estimated that the troops of Wu and Chu loved to make chopping the camp their business; that very night he divided his troops into two sections and placed them outside the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yong judged that southern troops favored night raids on enemy camps. That night he split his force in two and posted both divisions outside his own camp.

sentences.zh: 又以賊若夜來，必應於渡淮之所，以火記其淺處。

translations.literal: He also reasoned that if the enemy came by night they would surely ford the Huai where they had planned to cross, and he marked the shallow places with fire.
translations.idiomatic: He reasoned that if the enemy came at night they would cross where they had planned to ford the Huai, and he marked the shallow spots with fires.

sentences.zh: 永既設伏，乃密令人以瓠盛火，渡淮南岸，當深處置之，教之云：「若有火起，即亦然之。

translations.literal: After Yong had set his ambush, he secretly ordered men to fill gourds with fire, cross to the south bank of the Huai, and place them where the water was deep, instructing them: "If fires rise, then do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Once his ambush was in place, Yong secretly sent men with gourds of fire across to the south bank and set them where the water ran deep, with orders that if fires appeared anywhere, they were to light theirs as well.

sentences.zh: 」其夜，康祚、公政等果親率領，來斫永營。

translations.literal: " That night Kangzuo, Gongzheng, and the rest indeed personally led their troops and came to chop Yong's camp.
translations.idiomatic: " That night Kangzuo and Gongzheng led the attack in person against Yong's camp.

sentences.zh: 東西二伏夾擊之，康祚等奔趨淮水。

translations.literal: The eastern and western ambushes struck them from both sides; Kangzuo and the rest ran toward the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: The two ambush forces struck from east and west. Kangzuo's men fled toward the Huai.

sentences.zh: 火既競起，不能記其本濟，遂望永所置之火而爭渡焉。

translations.literal: Fires now rose in competition and they could not remember their original ford; they therefore looked toward the fires Yong had set and struggled to cross there.
translations.idiomatic: Fires blazed up everywhere, and in the confusion they could not find their own crossing. They rushed instead toward Yong's decoy fires and fought to ford there.

sentences.zh: 水深，溺死、斬首者數千級，生擒公政。

translations.literal: The water was deep; those drowned and beheaded numbered several thousand; Gongzheng was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: The water was deep. Thousands drowned or were cut down, and Gongzheng was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 康祚人馬墜淮，曉而獲其屍，斬首，并公政送京師。

translations.literal: Kangzuo's men and horses fell into the Huai; at dawn his corpse was recovered, his head was cut off, and together with Gongzheng they were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzuo and his horse went into the river. At dawn his body was recovered and beheaded. Both heads were sent to the capital with the captive Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 公政，岐州刺史超宗之從兄也。

translations.literal: Gongzheng was a cousin of Chao Zong, Inspector of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzheng was a cousin of Chao Zong, inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 時裴叔業率王茂先、李定等來侵楚王戍。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Shuye led Wang Maoxian, Li Ding, and others to invade the Prince of Chu's garrison.
translations.idiomatic: About that time Pei Shuye led Wang Maoxian, Li Ding, and others against the Prince of Chu's garrison fort.

sentences.zh: 永適還州，肅復令永討之。

translations.literal: Yong had just returned to the province; Su again ordered Yong to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had just returned to the province when Su again ordered him to take the field.

sentences.zh: [3]永將心腹一人馳詣楚王戍，至即令填塞外塹，夜伏戰士一千人於城外。

translations.literal: [3] Yong took one trusted confidant and galloped to the Prince of Chu's garrison; on arrival he immediately ordered the outer moat filled in and at night concealed one thousand fighting soldiers outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Yong took one trusted man and rode at full speed to the Prince of Chu's garrison. As soon as he arrived he ordered the outer ditch filled in and posted a thousand soldiers in ambush outside the walls that night.

sentences.zh: 曉而叔業等至，頓於城東，[4]列陳，將置長圍。

translations.literal: At dawn Shuye and the rest arrived, halted east of the city, [4] deployed battle arrays, and were about to set a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shuye arrived and made camp east of the city. [4] He drew up his battle lines and prepared to lay a full siege.

sentences.zh: 永所伏兵於左道擊其後軍，破之。

translations.literal: The soldiers Yong had concealed struck their rear army by the flank path and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's hidden troops struck the rear column on the flank and routed it.

sentences.zh: 叔業乃令將佐守所列之陳，自率精甲數千救之。

translations.literal: Shuye thereupon ordered his generals and assistants to hold the arrays they had deployed, while he personally led several thousand picked armored troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye left his officers to hold the line and led several thousand picked troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 永上門樓，觀叔業南行五六里許，便開門奮擊，遂摧破之。

translations.literal: Yong ascended the gate tower, watched Shuye go south five or six li, then opened the gates and struck with fury, and thereby crushed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: From the gate tower Yong watched Shuye march south for five or six li, then threw open the gates and charged, shattering the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 叔業進退失圖，於是奔走。

translations.literal: Shuye in advance and retreat lost his plan, and thereupon fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between advance and retreat with no plan left, Shuye broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 左右欲追之，永曰：「弱卒不滿三千，彼精甲猶盛，非力屈而敗，自墮吾計中耳。

translations.literal: Those at his side wished to pursue them; Yong said: "My weak soldiers number fewer than three thousand; their picked armor is still strong. It is not that they were defeated from exhausted strength—they have fallen into my plan.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged a pursuit. Yong said, "We have fewer than three thousand worn troops, while their elite armor is still strong. They did not break from weakness; they walked into my trap.

sentences.zh: 既不測我之虛實，足喪其膽。

translations.literal: Since they cannot fathom my emptiness and fullness, that is enough to destroy their courage.
translations.idiomatic: They still cannot gauge our true strength, and that alone is enough to break their nerve.

sentences.zh: 俘此足矣，何假逐之。

translations.literal: Capturing this much is sufficient; why borrow a pursuit?
translations.idiomatic: What we have taken is enough. Why chase them further?

sentences.zh: 」獲叔業傘扇鼓幕甲仗萬餘。

translations.literal: " They obtained more than ten thousand of Shuye's parasols, fans, drums, tent curtains, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: " They captured more than ten thousand of Shuye's parasols, fans, drums, tent hangings, suits of armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 兩月之中，遂獻再捷，高祖嘉之，遣謁者就豫州策拜永安遠將軍、鎮南府長史、汝南太守、貝丘縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Within two months he twice presented victories; Emperor Xiaowen praised him and sent a chamberlain to Yuzhou to invest him by edict as General of Distant Pacification for Yong'an, chief administrator of the southern garrison headquarters, Administrator of Runan, and founding baron of Beiqiu County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months he won two victories. Emperor Xiaowen was delighted and sent an envoy to Yuzhou to invest him as General of Distant Pacification for Yong'an, chief administrator of the southern headquarters, Administrator of Runan, and founding baron of Beiqiu with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖每歎曰：「上馬能擊賊，下馬作露布，唯傅脩期耳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen often sighed and said: "Mounted he can strike bandits; dismounted he can compose battlefield bulletins—only Fu Xiuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen would often say with admiration, "On horseback he can fight the enemy; on foot he can write a battlefield dispatch. Only Fu Xiuqi can do both.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業又圍渦陽，時高祖在豫州，遣永為統軍，與高聰、劉藻、成道益、任莫問等往救之。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye again besieged Woyang; at the time Emperor Xiaowen was in Yuzhou and sent Yong as army commander together with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Moqun, and others to go rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye besieged Woyang again. Emperor Xiaowen was then in Yuzhou and sent Yong as army commander with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Moqun, and others to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 軍將逼賊，永曰：「先深溝固壘，然後圖之。

translations.literal: The army was about to press close to the enemy; Yong said: "First dig deep ditches and fortify the ramparts, then plan the attack.
translations.idiomatic: As the army neared the enemy, Yong said, "Dig deep trenches and strengthen the ramparts first, then decide how to fight.

sentences.zh: 」聰等不從，裁營輜重，便擊之，一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Cong and the rest did not follow; they had barely encamped before managing the baggage train and then struck the enemy, and in one battle were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and the others refused. They had barely pitched camp and secured their baggage when they attacked, and were routed in a single engagement.

sentences.zh: 聰等棄甲，徑奔懸瓠。

translations.literal: Cong and the rest cast off their armor and ran straight to Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and his colleagues threw away their armor and fled straight to Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 永獨收散卒徐還，賊追至，又設伏擊之，挫其鋒銳。

translations.literal: Yong alone gathered the scattered soldiers and withdrew slowly; when the enemy pursued to them, he again set an ambush and struck them, blunting their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Yong alone gathered the scattered troops and withdrew in good order. When the pursuers caught up he ambushed them again and blunted their momentum.

sentences.zh: 四軍之兵，多賴之以免。

translations.literal: The troops of the four armies mostly relied on this to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the men in the four armies owed their escape to him.

sentences.zh: 永至懸瓠，高祖俱鎖之。

translations.literal: When Yong reached Xuanchi, Emperor Xiaowen had them all put in chains.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong reached Xuanchi, Emperor Xiaowen had the whole party put in chains.

sentences.zh: 聰、藻徙為邊民，永免官爵而已。

translations.literal: Cong and Zao were relocated as frontier commoners; Yong was merely stripped of office and noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and Zao were banished to the frontier as commoners. Yong was merely stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 不經旬日，詔曰：「脩期在後少有擒殺，可揚武將軍、汝陰鎮將，帶汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In less than ten days an edict said: "Xiuqi in the rear had some captures and kills; he may be made General Who Displays Might, garrison commandant of Ruyin, and concurrently Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days an edict arrived: "Xiuqi, fighting in the rear, still took some prisoners and kills. Appoint him General Who Displays Might, commandant of the Ruyin garrison, and concurrent Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 景明初，裴叔業將以壽春歸國，密通於永，永具表聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Pei Shuye was about to surrender Shouchun to the state; he secretly communicated with Yong, and Yong submitted a full memorial reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era Pei Shuye planned to surrender Shouchun to Wei. He contacted Yong in secret, and Yong reported the matter in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及將迎納，詔永為統軍，與楊大眼、奚康生等諸軍俱入壽春。

translations.literal: When the time came to welcome and receive him, an edict made Yong army commander; together with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and the other armies he all entered Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrender was to be received, the court appointed Yong army commander. He entered Shouchun with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and the other columns.

sentences.zh: 同日而永在後，故康生、大眼二人並賞列土，永唯清河男。

translations.literal: On the same day Yong was in the rear; therefore Kangsheng and Dayan were both rewarded with enfeoffed territory, while Yong received only the title Baron of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of entry Yong's column arrived last, so Kangsheng and Dayan were both rewarded with territorial fiefs while Yong received only the rank of Baron of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷將陳伯之侵逼壽春，沿淮為寇。

translations.literal: Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Bozhi pressed and threatened Shouchun, raiding along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Bozhi pressed on Shouchun and raided along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 時司徒、彭城王勰，廣陵侯元衍同鎮壽春，以九江初附，人情未洽，兼臺援不至，深以為憂。

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Education, the Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie, and the Marquis of Guangling Yuan Yan together garrisoned Shouchun. Because Jiujiang had just submitted and popular sentiment was not yet harmonious, and moreover capital reinforcements had not arrived, they were deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng, then Minister of Education, and Marquis Yan of Guangling were both stationed in Shouchun. With Jiujiang only recently submitted and the people still uneasy, and with no reinforcements yet from the capital, they were deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣永為統軍，領汝陰之兵三千人先援之。

translations.literal: An edict sent Yong as army commander, leading three thousand troops of Ruyin to go first in relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yong to take command and lead three thousand troops from Ruyin as the first relief column.

sentences.zh: 永總勒士卒，水陸俱下，而淮水口伯之防之甚固。

translations.literal: Yong mustered and led the soldiers, descending by both water and land, while at the Huai River mouth Bozhi's defenses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong marched his men by land and water alike, but Chen Bozhi held the mouth of the Huai in force.

sentences.zh: 永去二十餘里，牽船上汝南岸，以水牛挽之，直南趨淮，下船便渡。

translations.literal: Yong went more than twenty li away, drew the boats up on the south bank of the Ru, used water buffalo to haul them, rushed straight south toward the Huai, and on disembarking immediately crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong withdrew more than twenty li upstream, hauled his boats onto the south bank of the Ru, and had water buffalo drag them south toward the Huai. His men stepped ashore and crossed at once.

sentences.zh: 適上南岸，賊軍亦及。

translations.literal: Just as they reached the south bank, the rebel army also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached the south bank when the enemy came up as well.

sentences.zh: 會時已夜，永乃潜進，曉達壽春城下。

translations.literal: As it was already night, Yong advanced secretly and at dawn reached below the walls of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Night had fallen by then. Yong stole forward and at dawn was below the walls of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 勰、衍聞外有軍，共上門樓觀望，然不意永至，永免冑，乃信之，遂引永上。

translations.literal: Xie and Yan, hearing troops outside, together ascended the gate tower to look; they had not expected Yong to arrive. Yong removed his helmet, and they then trusted him and led Yong up.
translations.idiomatic: Xie and Yan heard troops outside and climbed the gate tower to look. They had not expected Yong. When he removed his helmet they recognized him and brought him up.

sentences.zh: 勰謂永曰：「北望以久，恐洛陽難復可見，不意卿能至也。

translations.literal: Xie said to Yong: "Gazing north so long, I feared Luoyang might never be seen again; I did not expect you could come.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said to Yong, "We have looked north so long that I feared we would never see Luoyang again. I did not think you could reach us."

sentences.zh: 」勰令永引軍入城。

translations.literal: " Xie ordered Yong to lead the army into the city.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Yong to bring his troops into the city.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「執兵被甲，固敵是求，若如教旨，便共殿下同被圍守，豈是救援之意？

translations.literal: Yong said: "Wielding weapons and wearing armor is fundamentally to seek the enemy; if we follow the instruction, we would together with Your Highness be besieged and held inside—how would that be the intent of rescue?
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, "We arm ourselves to find the enemy. If I followed your order we would sit under siege with you inside the walls. That is not how one relieves a city."

sentences.zh: 」遂孤軍城外，與勰并勢以擊伯之，頻有克捷。

translations.literal: " He then kept his army alone outside the city, joined forces with Xie to strike Bozhi, and frequently had victories.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept his force outside the walls, joined Xie, and attacked Chen Bozhi again and again with success.

sentences.zh: 中山王英之征義陽，永為寧朔將軍、統軍，當長圍遏其南門。

translations.literal: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan campaigned against Yiyang, Yong was General Who Pacifies the North and army commander, holding the long encirclement to block its southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Prince Ying of Zhongshan's campaign against Yiyang, Yong served as General Who Pacifies the North and army commander, blocking the southern gate at the head of the long encirclement.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍將馬仙琕連營稍進，規解城圍。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's general Ma Xianbi advanced camp by camp and planned to break the siege of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's general Ma Xianbi pushed his camps forward step by step, hoping to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 永謂英曰：「凶豎豕突，意在決戰。

translations.literal: Yong said to Ying: "The vicious rebel rushes like a boar; his intent is decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Ying, "This enemy is charging like a boar. He wants a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 雅山形要，宜早據之。

translations.literal: Mount Ya's terrain is strategic; we should seize it early.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Ya is the key ground. We must take it at once.

sentences.zh: 」英沉吟未决，永曰：「機者如神，難遇易失，今日不往，明朝必為賊有，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: " Ying hesitated and had not decided. Yong said: "Opportunity is like a spirit—hard to meet, easy to lose. If we do not go today, tomorrow the rebels will hold it; though we regret it, it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying hesitated. Yong said, "Chance is like a god—easy to miss, impossible to recall. If we do not go today, the enemy will hold that hill tomorrow, and regret will do us no good."

sentences.zh: 」英乃分兵，通夜築城於山上，遣統軍張懷等列陳於山下以防之。

translations.literal: " Ying then divided troops and through the night built a fort on the mountain, sending army commander Zhang Huai and others to deploy formations below the mountain to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: " Ying split his force and built a fort on the hill through the night, while Zhang Huai and other commanders formed up below to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 至曉，仙琕果至，懷等戰敗，築城者悉皆奔退，仙琕乘勝直趨長圍，義陽城人復出挑戰。

translations.literal: At dawn Xianbi indeed arrived; Huai and the others were defeated, and all who had been building the fort fled. Xianbi pressed his victory straight toward the long encirclement, and the people of Yiyang city again came out to challenge.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Ma Xianbi came as Yong had foreseen. Zhang Huai's line broke and the builders on the hill fled. Xianbi drove straight for the siege lines while the defenders of Yiyang sallied out again.

sentences.zh: 永乃分兵付長史賈思祖，令守營壘，自將馬步千人南逆仙琕。

translations.literal: Yong then divided troops and gave them to chief administrator Jia Sizu, ordering him to hold the camp and ramparts; he himself led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianbi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong left part of his force with Chief Administrator Jia Sizu to hold the camp and led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianbi.

sentences.zh: 擐甲揮戈，單騎先入，唯有軍主蔡三虎副之，餘人無有及者。

translations.literal: Donning armor and brandishing his halberd, he entered the formation alone on horseback; only army leader Cai Sanhu followed him, and no others could keep up.
translations.idiomatic: He buckled on his armor, raised his halberd, and charged in alone. Only the army leader Cai Sanhu could keep pace; no one else could catch him.

sentences.zh: 突陳橫過，賊射永洞其左股，永拔箭復入，遂大破之，斬仙琕子。

translations.literal: He burst through the formation crosswise; the rebels shot Yong and pierced his left thigh. Yong pulled out the arrow and entered again, then utterly defeated them and beheaded Xianbi's son.
translations.idiomatic: He cut across the enemy line. A bowshot pierced his left thigh; he pulled out the arrow and plunged back in, routed the enemy, and took the head of Xianbi's son.

sentences.zh: 仙琕燒營席卷而遁。

translations.literal: Xianbi burned his camps and fled, sweeping everything away.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi burned his camps and fled in haste.

sentences.zh: 英於陳謂永曰：「公傷矣，且還營。

translations.literal: Ying, amid the formation, said to Yong: "Sir, you are wounded; return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the battle Ying told Yong, "You are wounded. Go back to camp."

sentences.zh: 」永曰：「昔漢祖捫足，不欲人知。

translations.literal: " Yong said: "In former times the Han Founder clasped his foot and did not wish men to know.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "The Founder of Han once clutched his wounded foot so no one would know."

sentences.zh: 下官雖微，國家一帥，奈何使虜有傷將之名！

translations.literal: This humble official, though slight, is a commander of the state—how can we let the barbarians have the name of a wounded general!
translations.idiomatic: I may be a minor officer, but I am still a commander of the realm. I will not let the enemy boast that they wounded our general."

sentences.zh: 」遂與諸軍追之，極夜而返，時年七十餘矣。

translations.literal: " He then pursued with the various armies and returned only at the depth of night; he was then more than seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: " He rode on with the army until deep night before returning. He was already past seventy.

sentences.zh: 三軍莫不壯之。

translations.literal: The three armies all admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier in the three armies admired him.

sentences.zh: 義陽既平，英使司馬陸希道為露板，意謂不可，令永改之。

translations.literal: After Yiyang was pacified, Ying had his aide Lu Xidao draft a victory bulletin; he thought it unsatisfactory and had Yong revise it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiyang fell, Ying had his aide Lu Xidao draft a victory bulletin, found it wanting, and told Yong to rewrite it.

sentences.zh: 永亦不增文彩，直與之改陳列軍儀，處置形要而已。

translations.literal: Yong also did not add literary ornament; he simply revised the array of troops and military dispositions and disposition of strategic points, that alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yong added no flourish. He only reworked the order of battle, the disposition of units, and the key points of terrain.

sentences.zh: 而英深賞之，歎曰：「觀此經算，雖有金城湯池亦不能守矣。

translations.literal: Yet Ying deeply admired him and sighed: "Seeing this planning, even a city of metal walls and boiling moats could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Ying admired the result and sighed, "With planning like this, not even walls of bronze and moats of boiling water could hold a city."

sentences.zh: 」還京復封，永先有男爵，至是以品不累加，賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: " On returning to the capital he was enfeoffed again; Yong already had a baron's title, and on this occasion his rank was not increased by grades—only two thousand bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Back in the capital he was rewarded again. Yong already held a barony, so his rank was not raised further; he received two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 除太中大夫，行秦梁二州事，代邢巒鎮漢中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel, acting for the two provinces of Qin and Liang, replacing Xing Luan in garrisoning Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel and put in charge of Qin and Liang provinces, replacing Xing Luan as commander at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 永嘗登北邙，於平坦處奮矟躍馬，盤旋瞻望，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Yong once climbed Mount Beimang; on level ground he brandished his spear and leaped on his horse, wheeling and gazing about, with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Once on Mount Beimang he spurred his horse on open ground, spear in hand, circling and looking about as though he meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 遠慕杜預，近好李沖、王肅，欲葬附其墓，遂買左右地數頃，遺敕子叔偉曰：「此吾之永宅也。

translations.literal: From afar he admired Du Yu; in recent times he favored Li Chong and Wang Su and wished to be buried beside their tombs. He therefore bought several qing of land to left and right and left instructions to his son Shuwei: "This is my Yong estate.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Du Yu from old and lately favored Li Chong and Wang Su, hoping to lie near their graves. He bought several qing of land nearby and told his son Shuwei, "This is my eternal home."

sentences.zh: 」永妻賈氏留於本鄉，永至代都，娶妾馮氏，生叔偉及數女。

translations.literal: " Yong's wife, the Jia clan, remained in her native district; Yong reached the capital at Dai and took concubine Feng, who bore Shuwei and several daughters.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife Lady Jia stayed in their home district. At the northern capital he took concubine Feng, who bore Shuwei and several daughters.

sentences.zh: 賈後歸平城，無男，唯一女。

translations.literal: Jia later returned to Pingcheng; she had no sons, only one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia later returned to Pingcheng. She had no sons, only one daughter.

sentences.zh: 馮恃子事賈無禮，叔偉亦奉賈不順，賈常忿之。

translations.literal: Feng relied on her son and treated Jia without courtesy; Shuwei also served Jia disrespectfully, and Jia was often resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Feng relied on her son and treated Lady Jia rudely. Shuwei sided against Lady Jia as well, and she lived in constant anger.

sentences.zh: 馮先永亡，及永之卒，叔偉稱父命欲葬北邙。

translations.literal: Feng died before Yong; when Yong died, Shuwei claimed his father's command and wished to bury him on Beimang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng died before Yong. After Yong's death Shuwei claimed his father's wish to bury him on Beimang.

sentences.zh: 賈疑叔偉將以馮合葬，賈遂求歸葬永於所封貝丘縣。

translations.literal: Jia suspected Shuwei would bury Yong together with Feng; Jia therefore requested to return Yong for burial in his enfeoffed county of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia feared Shuwei would lay Yong beside Feng. She demanded that he be buried in his fief at Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 事經司徒，司徒胡國珍本與永同經征役，感其所慕，許叔偉葬焉。

translations.literal: The matter went before the Minister of Education; Minister Hu Guozhen had originally campaigned with Yong on the same campaigns, was moved by what Yong had admired, and permitted Shuwei to bury him there.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Ministry of Education. Minister Hu Guozhen had campaigned with Yong and, moved by Yong's own wishes, allowed Shuwei's burial plan.

sentences.zh: 賈乃邀訴靈太后，靈太后遂從賈意。

translations.literal: Jia then appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, and the Empress Dowager followed Jia's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, who sided with her.

sentences.zh: 事經朝堂，國珍理不能得，乃葬於東清河。

translations.literal: The matter reached the court hall; Guozhen could not prevail in argument and so the burial was at Dongqinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The dispute reached court and Guozhen lost the argument. Yong was buried in Dongqinghe.

sentences.zh: 又永昔營宅兆，葬父母於舊鄉，賈於此強徙之，與永同處，永宗親不能抑。

translations.literal: Moreover Yong had formerly arranged a grave site and buried his parents in his old district; Jia forcibly moved them here to lie with Yong, and Yong's clansmen could not restrain her.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had long before bought a grave plot and buried his parents in his home district. Lady Jia had them dug up and moved beside him, and his kin could not stop her.

sentences.zh: 葬已數十年矣，棺為桑棗根所遶束，去地尺餘，甚為周固，以斧斬斫，出之於坎，時人咸怪。

translations.literal: They had been buried for several decades; the coffins were wound and bound by mulberry and jujube roots, more than a foot from the ground, very firmly encircled. With axes they hewed and chopped and brought them out of the pit; people of the time all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: The coffins had lain for decades, gripped by mulberry and jujube roots a foot above the earth so tightly that men had to hew them free with axes. All who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 未三年而叔偉亡。

translations.literal: In less than three years Shuwei also died.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years Shuwei died as well.

sentences.zh: 叔偉，九歲為州主簿。

translations.literal: Shuwei at nine sui was a provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At nine sui Shuwei was already chief clerk of a province.

sentences.zh: 及長，膂力過人，彎弓三百斤，左右馳射，又能立馬上與人角騁。

translations.literal: When grown, his physical strength surpassed others; he could draw a bow of three hundred jin, shoot left and right while galloping, and could also wrestle on horseback with men.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, his strength was extraordinary. He drew a three-hundred-jin bow, shot on the move from either hand, and wrestled opponents from the saddle.

sentences.zh: 見者以為得永之武而不得永文也。

translations.literal: Observers thought he had Yong's martial prowess but not Yong's literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers said he had inherited Yong's valor but not his wit.

sentences.zh: 正光中，叔偉子豐生襲封。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, Shuwei's son Fengsheng succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era his son Fengsheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 傅豎眼，本清河人。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan was originally a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan came originally from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 七世祖伷。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor was You.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor was You.

sentences.zh: 伷子遘，石虎太常。

translations.literal: You's son Zun was Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: You's son Zun served Shi Hu as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祖父融南徙渡河，家于磐陽，為鄉閭所重。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rong moved south across the river and made his home at Panyang, where the village respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rong moved south across the Yellow River and settled at Panyang, where the countryside held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 性豪爽。

translations.literal: His nature was bold and open.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and open by nature.

sentences.zh: 有三子，靈慶、靈根、靈越，並有才力。

translations.literal: He had three sons—Lingqing, Linggen, and Lingyue—all with talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons—Lingqing, Linggen, and Lingyue—each gifted and formidable.

sentences.zh: 融以此自負，謂足為一時之雄。

translations.literal: Rong took pride in this and said he was enough to be a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rong took pride in them and believed himself the equal of any man of his day.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「吾昨夜夢：有一駿馬，無堪乘者，人曰：『何由得人乘之？

translations.literal: He once told someone: "Last night I dreamed: there was a fine steed, and none could ride it. Men said, 'How could one obtain someone to ride it?'
translations.idiomatic: He once told a neighbor, "Last night I dreamed of a fine horse that no one could mount. People asked how such a horse could ever be ridden."

sentences.zh: 』有一人對曰：『唯有傅靈慶堪乘此馬。

translations.literal: ' One man answered: 'Only Fu Lingqing can ride this horse.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, 'Only Fu Lingqing can ride that horse.'"

sentences.zh: 』又有弓一張，亦無人堪引，人曰：『唯有傅靈根可以彎此弓。

translations.literal: ' There was also one bow, and again no one could draw it. Men said, 'Only Fu Linggen can bend this bow.'
translations.idiomatic: There was also a bow no one could draw. They said, 'Only Fu Linggen can bend that bow.'"

sentences.zh: 』又有數紙文書，人皆讀不能解，人曰：『唯傅靈越可解此文。

translations.literal: ' There were also several sheets of written documents; everyone read them but could not understand. Men said, 'Only Fu Lingyue can interpret this text.'
translations.idiomatic: Then there were written sheets no one could read. They said, 'Only Fu Lingyue can read those texts.'"

sentences.zh: 』」融意謂其三子文武才幹堪以駕馭當世。

translations.literal: '" Rong meant that his three sons' civil and military talent and capacity were fit to master the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rong took this to mean his sons' civil and military gifts were fit to master their age.

sentences.zh: 常密謂鄉人曰：「汝聞之不？

translations.literal: He often secretly told villagers: "Have you heard?
translations.idiomatic: He often whispered to his neighbors, "Have you heard?"

sentences.zh: 鬲虫之子有三靈，此圖讖之文也。

translations.literal: The sons of the ge insect have three spirits—this is the text of a prophecy chart.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of the ge insect are three spirits—that is what the prophecy charts say."

sentences.zh: 」好事者然之，故豪勇之士多相歸附。

translations.literal: " Those who delighted in such things agreed, and so bold and brave men mostly attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Men who loved such omens believed him, and bold warriors flocked to his house.

sentences.zh: 劉駿將蕭斌、王玄謨寇碻磝，時融始死，玄謨強引靈慶為軍主。

translations.literal: Liu Jun's generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo attacked Que'ao; at the time Rong had just died, and Xuemo forcibly made Lingqing army leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jun's generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo attacked Que'ao, Rong had just died. Xuemo pressed Lingqing into service as army leader.

sentences.zh: 將攻城，攻車為城內所燒，靈慶懼軍法，詐云傷重，令左右輿之還營，遂與壯士數十騎遁還。

translations.literal: When they were about to assault the city, the assault towers were burned by those inside the city. Lingqing feared military law, falsely claimed grave wounds, had his attendants carry him back to camp in a litter, and then with several dozen brave horsemen fled back.
translations.idiomatic: As the assault began, defenders burned the siege engines. Fearful of punishment, Lingqing pretended grave wounds, had himself carried back to camp, then fled with a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 斌、玄謨命追之。

translations.literal: Bin and Xuemo ordered pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Xuemo ordered men after him.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「靈慶兄弟並有雄才，兼其部曲多是壯勇，如彭超、戶生之徒，皆一當數十人，援不虛發，不可逼也。

translations.literal: Attendants remonstrated: "The Lingqing brothers all have heroic talent, and moreover their followers are mostly stalwarts—men like Peng Chao and Hu Sheng, each a match for several tens of men, and their draws never miss. They cannot be pressed.
translations.idiomatic: His officers warned, "The brothers are all formidable, and their followers—men like Peng Chao and Hu Sheng—fight as ten against one and never miss with the bow. Do not press them."

sentences.zh: 不如緩之。

translations.literal: Better to go slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Better to let them go."

sentences.zh: 」玄謨乃止。

translations.literal: " Xuemo then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuemo halted the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 靈慶至家，遂與二弟匿於山澤之間。

translations.literal: Lingqing reached home and then with his two younger brothers hid in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqing reached home and hid in the hills with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 時靈慶從叔乾愛為斌法曹參軍，斌遣乾愛誘呼之，以腰刀為信，密令壯健者隨之，而乾愛不知斌之欲圖靈慶也。

translations.literal: At the time Lingqing's paternal cousin Qian'ai was Bin's aide of the law bureau; Bin sent Qian'ai to lure and summon him, using a waist knife as token, secretly ordering stalwart men to follow, while Qian'ai did not know Bin's intent to plot against Lingqing.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qian'ai served Xiao Bin as legal aide. Bin sent Qian'ai to summon Lingqing with a waist-knife as token and secretly ordered strong men to follow. Qian'ai did not know Bin meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 既至靈慶間，對坐未久，斌所遣壯士執靈慶殺之。

translations.literal: When they reached Lingqing's place and had sat facing each other not long, the stalwarts Bin had sent seized Lingqing and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely sat down when Bin's men seized Lingqing and killed him.

sentences.zh: 靈慶將死，與母崔訣，言「法曹殺人，不可忘也」。

translations.literal: As Lingqing was about to die, he took leave of his mother Cui and said, "The law aide killed a man—this must not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he bade farewell to his mother Lady Cui and said, "The law aide murdered me. Do not forget."

sentences.zh: 靈根、靈越奔河北。

translations.literal: Linggen and Lingyue fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen and Lingyue fled north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 靈越至京師，高宗見而奇之。

translations.literal: Lingyue reached the capital; Emperor Wencheng saw him and thought him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue reached the Wei capital. Emperor Wencheng saw him and was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 靈越因說齊民慕化，青州可平，高宗大悅。

translations.literal: Lingyue thereupon said the people of Qi yearned for transformation and Qingzhou could be pacified; Emperor Wencheng was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He told the court the people of Qi yearned for Wei rule and that Qingzhou could be taken. Emperor Wencheng was delighted.

sentences.zh: 拜靈越鎮遠將軍、青州刺史、貝丘子，鎮羊蘭城；

translations.literal: Lingyue was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Qingzhou, Baron of Beiqiu, garrisoning Yanglan Fort;
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue was made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Qingzhou, and Baron of Beiqiu, with his seat at Yanglan Fort.

sentences.zh: 靈根為臨齊副將，鎮明潛壘。

translations.literal: Linggen was deputy general of Linqi, garrisoning Mingqian Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen became deputy commander at Linqi and held Mingqian Rampart.

sentences.zh: 靈越北入之後，母崔氏遇赦免。

translations.literal: After Lingyue entered the north, his mother Lady Cui met an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingyue went north, his mother Lady Cui was spared by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 劉駿恐靈越在邊，擾動三齊，乃以靈越叔父琰為冀州治中，乾愛為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Liu Jun feared Lingyue on the frontier would disturb the Three Qi regions and therefore made Lingyue's uncle Yan chief administrator of Jizhou and Qian'ai Administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun feared Lingyue would stir the Three Qi and appointed his uncle Yan chief administrator of Jizhou and Qian'ai Administrator of Leling.

sentences.zh: 樂陵與羊蘭隔河相對，命琰遣其門生與靈越婢詐為夫婦投化以招之。

translations.literal: Leling and Yanglan faced each other across the river; he ordered Yan to send his student and Lingyue's maid to feign being husband and wife submitting in allegiance to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Leling lay across the river from Yanglan. Yan sent a student and Lingyue's maid to pose as husband and wife defecting in order to lure him back.

sentences.zh: 靈越與母分離思積，遂與靈根相要南走。

translations.literal: Lingyue, separated from his mother and sick with longing, then arranged with Linggen to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: Longing for his mother, Lingyue arranged with Linggen to flee south.

sentences.zh: 靈越與羊蘭奮兵相擊，乾愛遣船迎之，得免。

translations.literal: Lingyue fought fiercely with the troops at Yanglan; Qian'ai sent boats to welcome him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way out of Yanglan. Qian'ai sent boats and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 靈根差期，不得俱渡，臨齊人覺知，剉斬殺之。

translations.literal: Linggen missed the appointed time and could not cross together; the men of Linqi discovered it and hacked him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen missed the rendezvous. The garrison at Linqi caught him and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 乾愛出郡迎靈越，問靈根愆期之狀，而靈越殊不應答，但言不知而已。

translations.literal: Qian'ai went out of the commandery to welcome Lingyue and asked about Linggen's missing the appointed time; Lingyue utterly did not answer, only saying he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'ai rode out to meet Lingyue and asked why Linggen had been late. Lingyue would not answer and said only that he did not know.

sentences.zh: 乾愛不以為惡，敕左右出匣中烏皮袴褶，令靈越代所常服。

translations.literal: Qian'ai did not take it ill and ordered attendants to bring out from a case black leather trousers and jacket and had Lingyue replace his usual clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'ai took no offense and had attendants bring black leather coat and trousers from a chest for Lingyue to wear.

sentences.zh: 靈越言不須。

translations.literal: Lingyue said it was unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue refused.

sentences.zh: 乾愛云：「汝豈可著體上衣服見垣公也？

translations.literal: Qian'ai said: "How can you wear the clothes on your body to see Lord Yuan?
translations.idiomatic: Qian'ai said, "You cannot go before Lord Yuan in those rags."

sentences.zh: 」時垣護之為刺史。

translations.literal: " At the time Yuan Huzhi was governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi was then governor.

sentences.zh: 靈越奮聲言：「垣公！

translations.literal: Lingyue cried out loudly: "Lord Yuan!
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue shouted, "Lord Yuan!"

sentences.zh: 垣公！

translations.literal: Lord Yuan!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan!"

sentences.zh: 著此當見南方國主，豈垣公也。

translations.literal: Wearing this I should see the lord of the southern state—how would that be Lord Yuan?
translations.idiomatic: If I wear this I shall see the lord of the southern realm—not some Lord Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」竟不肯著。

translations.literal: " In the end he would not put them on.
translations.idiomatic: He would not put them on.

sentences.zh: 及至丹陽，劉駿見而禮之，拜員外郎、兗州司馬，帶魯郡，而乾愛亦遷青、冀司馬，帶魏郡。

translations.literal: When he reached Danyang, Liu Jun saw him and treated him with ceremony, appointing him Outer Gentleman and Sima of Yanzhou with concurrent charge of Lu commandery; Qian'ai was also transferred to Sima of Qing and Ji with concurrent charge of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Danyang Liu Jun received him with honor, made him Outer Gentleman and Sima of Yanzhou with charge of Lu, and moved Qian'ai to Sima of Qing and Ji with charge of Wei.

sentences.zh: 後二人俱還建康。

translations.literal: Later the two men both returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Later both men returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 靈越意恒欲為兄復讎，而乾愛初不疑防，知乾愛嗜雞肉葵菜食，乃為作之，下以毒藥，乾愛飯還而卒。

translations.literal: Lingyue constantly intended to avenge his brother, while Qian'ai at first did not suspect and guard against him. Knowing Qian'ai loved chicken with malva greens, he prepared it for him and put poison beneath; Qian'ai returned from his meal and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue still meant to avenge his brother. Qian'ai did not guard against him. Knowing Qian'ai loved chicken with malva greens, Lingyue cooked the dish for him with poison underneath. Qian'ai died after the meal.

sentences.zh: 後數年而靈越為太原太守，戍升城。

translations.literal: Several years later Lingyue was Administrator of Taiyuan, garrisoning Shengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Lingyue was Administrator of Taiyuan, stationed at Shengcheng.

sentences.zh: 後舉兵同劉駿子子勛，子勛以靈越為前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he raised troops with Liu Jun's son Zixun; Zixun made Lingyue Forward Army General.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose with Liu Jun's son Zixun, who made him Forward Army General.

sentences.zh: 子勛敗，靈越軍眾散亡，為劉彧將王廣之軍人所擒，厲聲曰：「我傅靈越也，汝得賊何不即殺！

translations.literal: Zixun was defeated; Lingyue's army scattered and fled. He was seized by soldiers of Liu Yu's general Wang Guangzhi and cried out loudly: "I am Fu Lingyue! You have caught a rebel—why not kill me at once!
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun fell, Lingyue's troops scattered. Wang Guangzhi's soldiers seized him. He shouted, "I am Fu Lingyue! You hold a rebel—why not kill me now?"

sentences.zh: 」廣之生送詣彧輔國府司馬劉勔。

translations.literal: " Guangzhi sent him alive to Liu Yu's aide of the Pacification Headquarters, Sima Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangzhi sent him alive to Liu Yu's Pacification Headquarters aide Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 勔躬自慰勞，詰其叛逆，對曰：「九州唱義，豈獨在我？

translations.literal: Yan personally consoled and comforted him and questioned him about rebellion; he answered: "The Nine Provinces raised the righteous cause—how could it be mine alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yan received him with courtesy and asked why he had rebelled. He answered, "The Nine Provinces rose in righteous cause. How could that be mine alone?"

sentences.zh: 」勔又問：「四方阻逆，無戰不擒，主上皆加以大恩，即其才用，卿何不早歸天闕，乃逃命草間乎？

translations.literal: " Yan again asked: "In the four quarters obstruction and rebellion—no battle without capture—the sovereign has all granted great favor, employing each man's talent. Why did you not early return to the heavenly court but flee for your life among the grasses?
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked again, "Rebels everywhere are taken in every battle, and the throne has shown great mercy, using each man's gifts. Why did you not return to court instead of hiding in the wild?"

sentences.zh: 」靈越答曰：「薛公舉兵淮北，威震天下，不能專任智勇，委付子姪，致敗之由，實在於此。

translations.literal: " Lingyue answered: "When the Duke of Xue raised troops north of the Huai, his might shook the realm; he could not entrust affairs solely to wisdom and courage but delegated to sons and nephews—the cause of defeat truly lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue replied, "When the Duke of Xue raised his army north of the Huai his power shook the realm, yet he could not rely on his own wit and valor alone and handed command to sons and nephews. That is why he failed."

sentences.zh: 然事之始末，備皆參預，人生歸於一死，實無面求活。

translations.literal: Yet from beginning to end of the affair I took part in all; human life returns to one death—I truly have no face to seek life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I took part from first to last. A man's life ends in death once, and I have no face left to beg for life."

sentences.zh: 」勔壯其意，送詣建康。

translations.literal: " Yan admired his spirit and sent him to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan admired his bearing and sent him on to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 劉彧欲加原宥，靈越辭對如一，終不回改，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu wished to grant pardon and clemency; Lingyue declined and answered as before, in the end not turning back or changing, and so was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu meant to spare him, but Lingyue answered as stubbornly as before and would not relent. He was executed.

sentences.zh: 豎眼，即靈越子也。

translations.literal: Shuyan was Lingyue's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan was Lingyue's son.

sentences.zh: 沉毅壯烈，少有父風。

translations.literal: Deep, resolute, and fiercely bold, in youth he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Grave, resolute, and fierce, he showed his father's spirit even as a youth.

sentences.zh: 入國，鎮南王肅見而異之，且奇其父節，傾心禮敬，表為參軍。

translations.literal: On entering the state, Prince Su of the Southern Garrison saw him and thought him unusual, and moreover admired his father's integrity; he devoted his heart in courteous respect and memorialized to make him aide.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered Wei, Prince Su of the Southern Garrison was struck by him and admired his father's integrity. Su treated him with full courtesy and had him appointed as an aide.

sentences.zh: 從肅征伐，累有戰功，稍遷給事中、步兵校尉、左中郎將，常為統軍，東西征伐。

translations.literal: Following Su on campaigns, he repeatedly had military achievement and was gradually promoted to attendant within the palace, colonel of foot soldiers, and Left General of the Household, often serving as army commander on eastern and western campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Su on campaign and won repeated distinction, rising to palace attendant, colonel of foot soldiers, and Left General of the Household, and often commanded armies in the east and west.

sentences.zh: 世宗時為建武將軍，討揚州賊破之，仍鎮於合肥，蕭衍民歸之者數千戶。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time he was General Who Establishes Martial Might; he attacked Yangzhou bandits and defeated them, then garrisoned at Hefei, and several thousand households of Xiao Yan's people submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was made General Who Establishes Martial Might, crushed rebels in Yangzhou, and garrisoned Hefei, where several thousand households of Liang subjects came over to him.

sentences.zh: 後武興氐楊集義反叛，推其兄子紹先為主，攻圍關城。

translations.literal: Later the Di of Wuxing, Yang Jiyi, rebelled, setting up his elder brother's son Shao as leader and attacking and besieging Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Di chieftain Yang Jiyi of Wuxing rebelled, enthroned his nephew Shao, and besieged Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史邢巒遣豎眼討之。

translations.literal: Governor of Liangzhou Xing Luan sent Shuyan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xing Luan of Liangzhou sent Fu Shuyan against him.

sentences.zh: 集義眾逆戰，頻破走之，乘勝追北，仍克武興。

translations.literal: Jiyi gathered his masses to meet in battle; Shuyan repeatedly defeated and drove him off, pressed the victory in pursuit to the north, and then recovered Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyi met him in force. Shuyan broke him again and again, pursued north, and recovered Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 還洛，詔假節，行南兗州事。

translations.literal: On returning to Luoyang, an edict lent him the staff of authority and put him in charge of the affairs of southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Luoyang he was given the staff of authority and put in charge of southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 豎眼善於綏撫，南人多歸之。

translations.literal: Shuyan was skilled at soothing settlement; many southerners attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan was gifted at winning people over, and many southerners came to his side.

sentences.zh: 轉昭武將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Displays Martial Might and Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Displays Martial Might and made Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 以州初置，境逼巴獠，給羽林虎賁三百人，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Because the province had just been established and its borders pressed the Ba and Liao, he was given three hundred guards of the imperial guard; his title was advanced to General of the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: The province was newly founded and bordered Ba and Liao territory, so he received three hundred imperial guards and was advanced to General of the Champions.

sentences.zh: 及高肇伐蜀，假豎眼征虜將軍、持節，領步兵三萬先討北巴。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Shuyan was lent the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians, with the staff of authority, leading thirty thousand foot soldiers to attack North Ba first.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao invaded Shu, Fu Shuyan was lent the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians with the staff of authority and led thirty thousand foot soldiers against North Ba.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍聞大軍西伐，遣其寧州刺史任太洪從陰平偷路入益州北境，欲擾動氐蜀，以絕運路。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan, hearing the great army was campaigning west, sent his Governor of Ningzhou Ren Taihong by the hidden route of Yinping to enter the northern border of Yizhou, intending to stir the Di and Shu and cut the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the western campaign, Xiao Yan sent his Governor of Ningzhou Ren Taihong through Yinping into northern Yizhou to stir up the Di and Shu and sever Wei's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 乘國諱班師，遂扇誘土民，奄破東洛、除口二戍，因此詐言南軍繼至，氐蜀信之，翕然從逆。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the state's mourning and withdrawal of troops, he then incited and enticed the native people, suddenly breaking the two garrisons of Dongluo and Chukou; on this basis he falsely said southern armies were arriving in succession, and the Di and Shu believed it and rose in revolt as one.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the court mourning and withdrawal, he incited the natives, stormed the garrisons at Dongluo and Chukou, and spread word that southern armies were coming. The Di and Shu believed him and rose together.

sentences.zh: 太洪率氐蜀數千圍逼關城，豎眼遣寧朔將軍成興孫討之。

translations.literal: Taihong led several thousand Di and Shu to press and besiege Guancheng; Shuyan sent General Who Pacifies the North Cheng Xingsun to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Taihong led thousands of Di and Shu against Guancheng. Fu Shuyan sent General Who Pacifies the North Cheng Xingsun to meet him.

sentences.zh: 軍次白護，太洪遣其輔國將軍任碩北等率眾一千，邀險拒戰，在虎徑南山連置三營。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baihu; Taihong sent his Pacification Headquarters general Ren Shuo and others north with a host of one thousand to seize difficult ground and resist battle, setting three camps in succession on the southern slopes of Tiger Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Baihu, Taihong sent Ren Shuo north with a thousand men to hold the passes, stringing three camps along the southern slopes of Tiger Pass.

sentences.zh: 興孫分遣諸統，隨便掩擊，皆破之。

translations.literal: Xingsun divided and sent the various commanders to strike as opportunity allowed; all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsun sent his commanders to strike wherever they could and broke every camp.

sentences.zh: 太洪又遣軍主邊昭等率氐蜀三千，攻逼興孫柵，興孫力戰，為流矢所中，死。

translations.literal: Taihong again sent army leader Bian Zhao and others leading three thousand Di and Shu to press and attack Xingsun's palisade; Xingsun fought fiercely, was struck by a stray arrow, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Taihong sent Bian Zhao with three thousand Di and Shu against Xingsun's stockade. Xingsun fought hard, took a stray arrow, and died.

sentences.zh: 豎眼又遣統軍姜喜、季元度從東嵠潛入，回出西崗，邀賊之後，表裏合擊，大破之，斬邊昭及太洪前部王隆護首。

translations.literal: Shuyan again sent army commanders Jiang Xi and Ji Yuandu to enter secretly from the eastern pass, wheel out from the western ridge, and intercept the rebels' rear; inside and outside joined in attack and utterly defeated them, beheading Bian Zhao and the heads of Taihong's forward division Wang Longhu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan sent Jiang Xi and Ji Yuandu through the eastern pass, swung around the western ridge, and struck the enemy rear. The converging attack routed them; Bian Zhao and Wang Longhu of Taihong's vanguard were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 於是太洪及關城五柵一時逃散。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taihong and the five palisades of Guancheng at one time scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Taihong and the five stockades at Guancheng fled at once.

sentences.zh: 豎眼性既清素，不營產業，衣食之外，俸祿粟帛皆以饗賜夷首，賑恤士卒。

translations.literal: Shuyan's nature was pure and plain; he did not manage estates. Beyond food and clothing, salary grain and silk were all used to feast and grant to tribal chiefs and relieve soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan lived plainly and built no estates. Beyond his own needs he spent salary grain and silk on tribal leaders and his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 撫蜀人以恩信為本，保境安民，不以小利侵竊。

translations.literal: In soothing the people of Shu he took benevolence and trust as foundation, guarded the borders and settled the people, and did not invade or steal for small profit.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled Shu on benevolence and trust, guarded the borders, and would not steal even small gains.

sentences.zh: 有掠蜀民入境者，皆移送還本土。

translations.literal: When there were those who plundered Shu people entering the borders, all were transferred back to their native lands.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who seized Shu subjects across the border was made to send them home.

sentences.zh: 撿勒部下，守宰肅然。

translations.literal: He inspected and restrained subordinates; magistrates and prefects were all in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his subordinates in strict order, and local officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 遠近雜夷相率款謁，仰其德化，思為魏民矣。

translations.literal: Far and near, mixed tribes in succession came to offer allegiance, looking up to his virtue and transformation, wishing to become Wei's people.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes far and near came to submit, drawn by his virtue and eager to become subjects of Wei.

sentences.zh: 是以蜀民請軍者旬月相繼。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of Shu requesting troops came month after month in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shu families asking for Wei garrisons arrived month after month.

sentences.zh: 世宗甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，屢請解州，乃以元法僧代之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign he repeatedly requested to relinquish the province, and Yuan Faseng was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign he repeatedly asked to leave office, and Yuan Faseng was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 益州民追隨戀泣者數百里。

translations.literal: The people of Yizhou followed him in pursuit, weeping with attachment, for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: People of Yizhou followed him for hundreds of li, weeping as he left.

sentences.zh: 至洛，拜征虜將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: On reaching Luoyang he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將趙祖悅入屯硤石，以逼壽春。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his general Zhao Zuyue to enter and garrison Xiashi, pressing Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Zhao Zuyue to occupy Xiashi and threaten Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍崔亮討之，以豎眼為持節、鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: Pacification Headquarters General Cui Liang attacked him and made Shuyan holder of the staff and army secretary of the Southern Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang of the Pacification Headquarters attacked him and made Fu Shuyan holder of the staff and army secretary of the Southern Garrison.

sentences.zh: 法僧既至，大失民和。

translations.literal: After Faseng arrived, he greatly lost the harmony of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once Faseng took office he quickly lost the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其信武將軍、衡州刺史張齊因民心之怨，[5]入寇晉壽，頻陷葭萌、小劍諸戍，進圍州城。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Hengzhou Zhang Qi, because of the people's resentment, [5] to invade Jinshou, frequently capturing the garrisons of Jiameng and Xiaojian and the rest, and advancing to besiege the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Hengzhou Zhang Qi to exploit popular resentment Note marker [5] and invade Jinshou. He took Jiameng, Xiaojian, and other posts and advanced to besiege the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以西南為憂，乃驛徵豎眼於淮南。

translations.literal: The court, taking the southwest as a worry, then by post urgently summoned Shuyan from Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed for the southwest, the court summoned Fu Shuyan posthaste from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 既至，以為右將軍、益州刺史，尋加散騎常侍、平西將軍、假安西將軍、西征都督，率步騎三千以討張齊。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was made Right General and Governor of Yizhou; soon he was also added Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General Who Pacifies the West, and lent General Who Pacifies the West and Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief, leading three thousand foot and horse to attack Zhang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was made Right General and Governor of Yizhou, then Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General Who Pacifies the West, and lent commander of the western campaign with three thousand troops against Zhang Qi.

sentences.zh: 給銅印千餘，須有假職者，聽六品已下板之。

translations.literal: He was given more than a thousand bronze seals; wherever there was need for acting office, those of sixth rank and below might be appointed by board.
translations.idiomatic: He received more than a thousand bronze seals and authority to appoint acting officers of sixth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 豎眼既出梁州，衍冠軍將軍勾道侍、梁州刺史王太洪等十餘將所在拒塞，[6]豎眼三日之中，轉戰二百餘里，甲不去身，頻致九捷。

translations.literal: After Shuyan left Liangzhou, Yan's General of the Champions Gou Daoshi, Governor of Liangzhou Wang Taihong, and more than ten generals everywhere blocked and obstructed, [6] and in three days Shuyan fought in more than two hundred li, armor not leaving his body, frequently achieving nine victories.
