translations.idiomatic: Leaving Liangzhou, Fu Shuyan met more than a dozen Liang commanders including Gou Daoshi and Wang Taihong Note marker [6] blocking his path. In three days he fought over two hundred li without doffing his armor and won nine victories.

sentences.zh: 土民統軍席廣度等處處邀擊，斬太洪及衍征虜將軍楊伏錫等首。

translations.literal: Native commanders such as Xi Guangdu everywhere intercepted and struck, beheading Taihong and the heads of Yan's General Who Subdues the Barbarians Yang Fuxi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Local commanders such as Xi Guangdu harried the enemy on every side. Taihong and Yang Fuxi were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 張齊引兵西退，遂奔葭萌。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi led his troops in retreat to the west and then fled to Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi drew west and fled to Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 蜀民聞豎眼復為刺史，人人喜悅，迎於路者日有百數。

translations.literal: The people of Shu, hearing Shuyan was again governor, each rejoiced; those welcoming him on the road numbered a hundred each day.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu heard Fu Shuyan was governor again, the people rejoiced. A hundred a day came out to welcome him on the road.

sentences.zh: 豎眼至州，白水已東，民皆寧業。

translations.literal: When Shuyan reached the province, east of the White River the people all settled in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the province, all east of the White River returned to peaceful livelihood.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍信義將軍、都統白水諸軍事楊興起，征虜將軍李光宗襲據白水舊城。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiao Yan's Trustworthy and Righteous General and overall commander of military affairs at White River Yang Xingqi, and General Who Subdues the Barbarians Li Guangzong, had raided and seized the old city of White River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Xingqi, Liang's Trustworthy and Righteous General commanding at White River, and Li Guangzong, General Who Subdues the Barbarians, had seized the old city of White River.

sentences.zh: 豎眼遣虎威將軍強虬與陰平王楊太赤率眾千餘，夜渡白水，旦而交戰，大敗賊軍，斬興起首，克復舊城。

translations.literal: Shuyan sent Tiger Might General Qiang Qiu together with King of Yinping Yang Taichi leading more than a thousand to cross the White River at night; at dawn they joined battle and utterly defeated the rebel army, beheading Xingqi's head and recovering the old city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan sent Qiang Qiu and King Yang Taichi of Yinping with more than a thousand men to cross the White River by night. At dawn they routed the enemy, took Xingqi's head, and recovered the old city.

sentences.zh: 又遣統軍傅曇表等大破衍寧朔將軍王光昭於陰平。

translations.literal: He again sent army commander Fu Yanbiao and others to utterly defeat Yan's General Who Pacifies the North Wang Guangzhao at Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Yanbiao and others to crush Wang Guangzhao, Liang's General Who Pacifies the North, at Yinping.

sentences.zh: 張齊仍阻白水，屯寇葭萌。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi still blocked the White River and garrisoned raiding at Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi still held the White River and raided from Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 豎眼分遣諸將水陸討之。

translations.literal: Shuyan divided and sent the various generals to attack by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan sent his generals against him by land and water.

sentences.zh: 齊遣其寧朔將軍費忻督步騎二千逆來拒戰，軍主陳洪起力戰破之，乘勝追奔，遂臨夾谷三柵。

translations.literal: Qi sent his General Who Pacifies the North Fei Xin to supervise two thousand foot and horse coming in opposition to battle; army leader Chen Hongqi fought fiercely and broke them, pressed the victory in pursuit, and then approached the three palisades of Jiagu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Fei Xin with two thousand horse and foot to meet them. Chen Hongqi broke his line, pursued, and came up to the three stockades at Jiagu.

sentences.zh: 統軍胡小虎四面攻之，三柵俱潰。

translations.literal: Army commander Hu Xiaohu attacked from four sides; the three palisades all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiaohu attacked from four sides and all three stockades fell.

sentences.zh: 張齊親率驍勇二萬餘人與諸軍交戰，豎眼命諸統帥同時奮擊。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi personally led more than twenty thousand stalwarts to join battle with the armies; Shuyan ordered the various commanders to strike together at one time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi led more than twenty thousand picked troops into battle. Fu Shuyan ordered a simultaneous assault by all his commanders.

sentences.zh: 軍主許暢斬衍雄信將軍牟興祖，軍主孔領周射齊中足，於是大破賊軍，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Army leader Xu Chang beheaded Yan's Trustworthy Faith General Mou Xingzu; army leader Kong Lingzhou shot Qi in the foot; thereupon the rebel army was utterly defeated and captures were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chang slew Mou Xingzu; Kong Lingzhou shot Qi in the foot. The enemy army was routed with heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 齊乃柵於虎頭山下，賊帥任令崇屯據西郡。

translations.literal: Qi then palisaded below Tiger Head Mountain; rebel commander Ren Lingchong garrisoned and held Xijun.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fortified himself below Tiger Head Mountain while Ren Lingchong held Xijun.

sentences.zh: 豎眼復遣討之，令崇棄眾夜遁。

translations.literal: Shuyan again sent to attack; Lingchong abandoned his troops and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan attacked again; Lingchong abandoned his force and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 乃進討齊，破其二柵，斬首萬餘，齊被重創，奔竄而退。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Qi, broke his two palisades, beheaded more than ten thousand; Qi received grave wounds and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Qi, stormed two stockades, and took more than ten thousand heads. Qi was badly wounded and fled.

sentences.zh: 小劍、大劍賊亦捐城西走，益州平。

translations.literal: The rebels at Xiaojian and Dajian also abandoned the cities and fled west; Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons at Xiaojian and Dajian also abandoned their posts. Yizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 靈太后璽書慰勞，賜驊騮馬一匹，寶劍一口。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent a letter under the imperial seal to comfort and reward him, granting one piebald horse and one precious sword.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent an imperial letter of praise, a piebald horse, and a precious sword.

sentences.zh: 豎眼表求解州，不許，復轉安西將軍、岐州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Shuyan memorialized requesting to relinquish the province; it was not permitted, and he was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qi Province, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan asked to leave Yizhou but was refused. He was made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qi, retaining his attendant title.

sentences.zh: 仍轉梁州刺史，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Governor of Liangzhou, attendant and general as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Governor of Liangzhou with the same attendant rank and general title.

sentences.zh: 梁州之人既得豎眼為牧，人咸自賀。

translations.literal: The people of Liangzhou, having obtained Shuyan as governor, all congratulated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liangzhou rejoiced to have Fu Shuyan as their governor.

sentences.zh: 而豎眼至州，遇患不堪綜理，其子敬紹險暴不仁，聚貨耽色，甚為民害，遠近怨望焉。

translations.literal: Yet when Shuyan reached the province he fell ill and could not manage affairs; his son Jingshao was cruel and violent without benevolence, amassed goods and indulged in lust, greatly harming the people, and far and near resented and looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: But when Fu Shuyan reached the province he fell ill and could not govern. His son Jingshao was cruel, greedy, and dissolute, and the province groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 尋假鎮軍將軍、都督梁西益巴三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was lent General Who Pacifies the Army and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for Liang, western Yi, and Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was lent General Who Pacifies the Army and supreme commander over Liang, western Yi, and Ba.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其北梁州長史錫休儒、司馬魚和、上庸太守姜平洛等十軍，率眾三萬，入寇直城。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his chief administrator of northern Liangzhou Xi Xiuru, aide Sima Yu He, Administrator of Shangyong Jiang Pingluo, and ten armies, leading a host of thirty thousand, to invade Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Xi Xiuru, Yu He, Jiang Pingluo, and ten columns with thirty thousand men against Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 豎眼遣敬紹總眾赴之，倍道而進，至直城，而賊襲據直口。

translations.literal: Shuyan sent Jingshao to command the masses to go to meet them, marching day and night; when they reached Zhicheng the rebels had already seized Zhikou by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan sent Jingshao ahead at forced march. At Zhicheng the enemy had already seized Zhikou.

sentences.zh: 敬紹以賊斷歸路，督兼統軍高徹、吳和等與賊決戰，大破之，擒斬三千餘人，休儒等走還魏興。

translations.literal: Jingshao, because the rebels had cut the return route, supervised concurrent army commanders Gao Che, Wu He, and others to join the rebels in decisive battle, utterly defeated them, captured and beheaded more than three thousand, and Xiuru and the others fled back to Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: With his retreat cut, Jingshao led Gao Che, Wu He, and others into a decisive battle, routed the enemy, and took more than three thousand heads. Xiuru fled back to Weixing.

sentences.zh: 敬紹頗覽書傳，微有膽力，而奢淫倜儻，輕為殘害。

translations.literal: Jingshao had read somewhat in books and records and had slight courage and strength, yet was extravagant, dissolute, and unrestrained, lightly committing cruel harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshao had some learning and a little courage, but he was extravagant and cruel by habit.

sentences.zh: 又見天下多事，陰懷異圖，欲杜絕四方，擅據南鄭，令其妾兄唐崐崙扇攪於外，聚眾圍城，敬紹謀為內應。

translations.literal: He also saw that under heaven many affairs were in turmoil and secretly harbored a different design, wishing to cut off the four quarters and exclusively hold Nan Zheng, ordering his concubine's elder brother Tang Kunlun to stir up trouble outside, gathering masses to besiege the city, with Jingshao plotting to act as inner agent.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm in turmoil, he plotted to hold Nan Zheng alone, set his concubine's brother Tang Kunlun to raise a siege outside, and meant to open the gates from within.

sentences.zh: 賊圍既合，其事泄露，在城兵武執敬紹，白豎眼而殺之。

translations.literal: When the rebel siege had closed, the matter was leaked; soldiers and martial officers in the city seized Jingshao, reported to Shuyan, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege closed the plot leaked. The garrison seized Jingshao, reported to Fu Shuyan, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 豎眼耻恚發疾，遂卒。

translations.literal: Shuyan, shamed and resentful, fell ill and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan, shamed and enraged, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈征東將軍、吏部尚書、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East, Minister of Personnel, and Governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，重贈散騎常侍、車騎將軍、司空公、相州刺史，開國如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he was again posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General of the Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou; his state founding remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously raised to Attendant Cavalier at Leisure, General of the Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Governor of Xiangzhou, with his fief unchanged.

sentences.zh: 長子敬和，敬和弟敬仲，並好酒薄行，傾側勢家。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jinghe and Jinghe's younger brother Jingzhong both loved wine and had slight conduct, leaning toward powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jinghe and younger son Jingzhong were both drunkards of poor character who curried favor with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 敬和，歷青州鎮遠府長史。

translations.literal: Jinghe successively served as chief administrator of the Pacification Headquarters of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe served as chief administrator of the Qingzhou Pacification Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，復為益州刺史，朝廷以其父有遺惠故也。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaozhuang's time he was again made Governor of Yizhou because the court considered that his father had left lingering kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he was again made Governor of Yizhou in memory of his father's kindness to the province.

sentences.zh: 至州，聚斂無已，好酒嗜色，遠近失望。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he amassed without end, loved wine and indulged in lust; far and near were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: At his arrival he extorted without end and gave himself to wine and women until the province despaired of him.

sentences.zh: 仍為蕭衍將樊文熾攻圍，敬和以城降，送於江南。

translations.literal: He was then besieged by Xiao Yan's general Fan Wench, and Jinghe surrendered the city and was sent to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wench of Liang besieged him; Jinghe surrendered the city and was sent south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 後衍以齊獻武王威德日廣，令敬和還國，以申和通之意。

translations.literal: Later Yan, because Prince Xianwu of Qi Wei's might and virtue grew daily, ordered Jinghe to return to the state to express the intent of harmony and communication.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Prince Xianwu of Qi's power grew, Liang sent Jinghe back to Wei as a gesture of reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 久之，除北徐州刺史，復以耽酒為土賊掩襲，棄城走。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Governor of northern Xuzhou; again because of drunkenness he was surprised by local bandits, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made Governor of northern Xuzhou, but drunkenness led bandits to surprise him and he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 徵詣廷尉，遇恩免，遂廢棄卒於家。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Minister of Justice, he met grace and was pardoned, then was discarded and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Called before the Minister of Justice, he was pardoned by grace, then lived out his days in obscurity at home.

sentences.zh: 乾愛子三寶，與房法壽等同効盤陽，[7]賜爵貝丘子。

translations.literal: Qian'ai's son Sanbao, together with Fang Fashou and others, together rendered merit at Panyang, [7] and was granted the title Baron of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'ai's son Sanbao, with Fang Fashou and others, won merit at Panyang Note marker [7] and was ennobled Baron of Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 三寶弟法獻，高祖初南叛，為蕭鸞右中郎將、直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Sanbao's younger brother Faxian, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen, defected south and became Xiao Luan's Right General of the Household and general of the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbao's younger brother Faxian defected south early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign and became Xiao Luan's Right General of the Household and inner-guard commander.

sentences.zh: 從崔慧景至鄧城，為官軍所殺。

translations.literal: Following Cui Huijing to Dengcheng, he was killed by the government army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cui Huijing to Dengcheng and was killed by the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 琰曾孫文驥，勇果有將領之才。

translations.literal: Yan's great-grandson Wenji was brave and resolute and had the talent of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's great-grandson Wenji was bold and had true commander's gifts.

sentences.zh: 隨豎眼征伐，累有軍功，自強弩將軍出為琅邪戍主。

translations.literal: Following Shuyan on campaigns, he repeatedly had military achievement; from General of Strong Crossbows he went out as garrison commander of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Shuyan on campaign with repeated distinction, rose from General of Strong Crossbows, and became garrison commander of Langye.

sentences.zh: 朐山內附，徐州刺史盧昶遣文驥守朐山，樵米既竭，而昶軍不進。

translations.literal: When Qushan submitted inward, Governor of Xuzhou Lu Chang sent Wenji to guard Qushan; firewood and grain were exhausted, yet Chang's army did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Qushan came over to Wei, Lu Chang of Xuzhou sent Wenji to hold it. Fuel and grain ran out while Chang's relief army never came.

sentences.zh: 文驥遂棄母妻，以城降蕭衍。

translations.literal: Wenji then abandoned mother and wife and surrendered the city to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji abandoned his mother and wife and surrendered the city to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 後大以南貨賂光州刺史羅衡，衡為渡其母妻。

translations.literal: Later he greatly used southern goods to bribe Governor of Guangzhou Luo Heng; Heng crossed over his mother and wife for him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he bribed Luo Heng, Governor of Guangzhou, with southern goods until Heng ferried his mother and wife across to him.

sentences.zh: 李神，恒農人。

translations.literal: Li Shen was a man of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen came from Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 父洪之，秦益二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi was Governor of Qin and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongzhi had been Governor of Qin and Yi.

sentences.zh: 神少有膽略，以氣尚為名。

translations.literal: Shen in youth had courage and stratagem and was famous for valorous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had courage and resource even in youth and was known for his fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 早從征役，其從兄崇深所知賞。

translations.literal: He early followed campaigns; his cousin Chong knew and appreciated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He saw action early, and his cousin Chong thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 累遷威遠將軍、新蔡太守，領建安戍主。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Overawes the Distant and Administrator of Xincai, concurrently garrison commander of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Overawes the Distant and Administrator of Xincai, with concurrent command of the Jian'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 轉寧遠將軍、陳留太守，領狄丘戍主。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Chenliu, concurrently garrison commander of Diqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Chenliu, commanding the Diqiu garrison.

sentences.zh: 頻有軍功，封長樂縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly had military achievement and was enfeoffed as founding baron of Changle County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated victories won him the founding barony of Changle with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、驍騎將軍、直閤將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, General of Valiant Cavalry, and General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Subdues the Barbarians, General of Valiant Cavalry, and general of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍將趙祖悅率眾據硤石，神為別將，率揚州水軍受刺史李崇節度，與都督崔亮、行臺僕射李平等攻硤石克之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's general Zhao Zuyue led a host to hold Xiashi; Shen was a separate commander, leading Yangzhou naval forces under the regulation of Governor Li Chong, and together with Commander-in-Chief Cui Liang and Acting Secretariat Master of Documents Li Ping attacked Xiashi and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zuyue of Liang held Xiashi, Shen served as a detached commander of Yangzhou naval forces under Li Chong, and with Cui Liang and Li Ping took the city.

sentences.zh: 進平北將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，行相州事，尋正，加撫軍將軍，假鎮東將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he acted for the affairs of Xiangzhou; soon he was made regular, and added General Who Comforts the Army, lent General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he acted as governor of Xiangzhou, was soon confirmed, and was given General Who Comforts the Army, lent General Who Pacifies the East, and made Grand Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was made General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮充斥，民多逃散。

translations.literal: At the time Ge Rong filled the land; the people mostly scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's rebels were everywhere and the people fled in masses.

sentences.zh: 先是，州將元鑒反叛引賊，後都督源子邕、裴衍戰敗被害，朝野憂惶，人不自保。

translations.literal: Earlier the provincial general Yuan Jian had rebelled and drawn in bandits; afterward Commander-in-Chief Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan were defeated in battle and killed. Court and countryside were anxious and fearful; no one could protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the provincial commander Yuan Jian had rebelled and invited the rebels in. Later Commander Yuan Ziyin and Pei Yan were defeated and killed. The court and country were terrified and no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 而神志氣自若，撫勞兵民，小大用命。

translations.literal: Yet his spirit and bearing were calm as ever; he comforted and encouraged soldiers and people, and great and small obeyed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shen remained calm in spirit, comforted soldiers and civilians alike, and won obedience from every rank.

sentences.zh: 既而葛榮盡銳攻之，久不能克。

translations.literal: Then Ge Rong attacked with all his elite strength for a long time but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong then threw his best troops against the city for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 會尒朱榮擒葛榮於鄴西，事平。

translations.literal: It happened that Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong west of Ye; the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong west of Ye and the crisis ended.

sentences.zh: 除車騎將軍，以功進爵為公，增邑八百，通前一千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Cavalry; for merit his rank was advanced to duke, fief increased by eight hundred, totaling one thousand households with the previous.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Cavalry and, for his service, advanced to duke with eight hundred added households, bringing his fief to one thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，莊帝北巡，以神為侍中，又除殿中尚書，仍行相州事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Emperor Xiaozhuang toured the north; Shen was made attendant within the palace and also appointed Master of Writings in the Palace, still acting for the affairs of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Emperor Xiaozhuang went north on tour. Shen was made palace attendant and Master of Writings in the Palace while still governing Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，改封安康郡開國公，加封五百戶。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, his enfeoffment was changed to founding duke of Ankang commandery, with five hundred households added to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the palace, Shen was re-enfeoffed as founding duke of Ankang with five hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，進驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、相州大中正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai he was advanced to General of the Valiant Cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and chief rectifier of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai year one he was advanced to General of the Valiant Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and made chief rectifier of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中薨。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Yongxi era.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，賜使持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping he was granted the staff of authority, attendant within the palace, General of the Valiant Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year one he was posthumously granted the staff of authority, made attendant within the palace, General of the Valiant Cavalry, Minister of Education, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子士約，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shiyue succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyue inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, noble ranks were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, noble ranks were reduced as usual.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：劉藻、傅永、豎眼文武器幹，知名於時。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, and Shuyan had civil and military talent and capacity and were famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, and Fu Shuyan were famed in their day for civil and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 豎眼加以撫邊導俗，風化尤美，方之二子，固以優乎？

translations.literal: Shuyan moreover in soothing the frontier and guiding custom had especially beautiful transformation; compared with the two sons, is he not clearly superior?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan, who also pacified the frontier and guided custom, was especially admired for his civilizing work. Set beside the other two, was he not plainly their superior?

sentences.zh: 抑又魏世之良牧。

translations.literal: He was moreover a good governor of the Wei age.
translations.idiomatic: He ranks among the fine governors of the Wei dynasty as well.

sentences.zh: 李神據危城，當大難，其氣概亦足稱焉。

translations.literal: Li Shen held a perilous city and faced great calamity; his spirit and bearing are also enough to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen held a desperate city through great peril; his bearing too deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 在任八年遷離城鎮將 按下文云「太和中，改鎮為岐州」。

translations.literal: After eight years in office he was transferred to garrison commander of Licheng—according to the text below, "In the Taihe era the garrison was changed to Qi Province."
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "After eight years in office he was transferred to garrison commander of Licheng"—the passage below states, "In the Taihe era the garrison was changed to Qi Province."

sentences.zh: 查卷一０六下地形志下岐州條注云：「治雍城鎮。

translations.literal: Checking the commentary to the entry for Qi Province in the Treatise on Geography, juan 106B, it says: "Administered from Yongcheng Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: The commentary on Qi Province in the Treatise on Geography, juan 106B, reads, "Administered from Yongcheng Garrison."

sentences.zh: 」自漢以來，即置雍縣，地由雍水得名，別無所謂「離城」。

translations.literal: " Since Han times Yong County had been established; the place took its name from the Yong River—there is nothing called "Licheng."
translations.idiomatic: " Since Han times the seat had been Yong County, named for the Yong River. There is no place called "Licheng."

sentences.zh: 這裏「離」字顯為「雍」之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character li is clearly a corruption for yong.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character for "Li" is plainly a corruption of "Yong."

sentences.zh: 但上文已稱他「遷龍驤將軍雍城鎮將」，所謂「在任八年」，即指在雍城鎮將之任，怎麼能以雍城鎮將遷雍城鎮將呢？

translations.literal: But above he is already said to have been "transferred to General of the Flying Dragon and garrison commander of Yongcheng"; the phrase "eight years in office" refers to his tenure as garrison commander of Yongcheng—how could he be transferred from Yongcheng garrison commander to Yongcheng garrison commander?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the text above already calls him General of the Flying Dragon and garrison commander of Yongcheng. "Eight years in office" must mean that post—so how could he be promoted from Yongcheng commander to Yongcheng commander?

sentences.zh: 而且疑問尚不止鎮名之異。

translations.literal: Moreover the doubts are not limited to the difference in the garrison name.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is not only the garrison name.

sentences.zh: 上文於劉藻遷雍城鎮將後，說「雍州人王叔保等三百人表乞藻為騃奴戍主。

translations.literal: Above, after Liu Zao was transferred to Yongcheng garrison commander, it says "Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao and others memorialized begging that Zao be made garrison commander of Yinu.
translations.idiomatic: Above, after Liu Zao became Yongcheng garrison commander, the text says, "Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao asked that Zao be made garrison commander of Yinu."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「選曹已用人，藻有惠政，自宜他敍。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The selection office has already appointed someone; Zao has benevolent government and should receive another posting.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "The selection office has already filled the post. Zao's benevolent rule deserves another appointment."

sentences.zh: 」戍主品級比鎮將低，王叔保等是表示對他好感才乞求任他為戍主的，怎麼會要他降級調任呢？

translations.literal: " The rank of garrison commander was lower than that of garrison commander of a major post; Wang Shubao and the others were expressing goodwill and therefore begged that he be made garrison commander—how could they want him demoted and transferred?
translations.idiomatic: " A garrison command was lower than a major garrison command. The petitioners were showing goodwill, not asking for his demotion—so why would they request a lesser post?

sentences.zh: 細觀此段，實是文字錯簡，又有衍文。

translations.literal: Examining this passage closely, it is in fact misplaced text with redundant wording.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: On close reading this passage is disordered and contains redundant text.

sentences.zh: 上文「遷龍驤將軍、雍城鎮將」至「羣氐震慴」四十二字當在「在任八年」下。

translations.literal: The forty-two characters above from "transferred to General of the Flying Dragon, garrison commander of Yongcheng" through "all the Di were shaken in awe" should stand below "eight years in office."
translations.idiomatic: The forty-two characters from "transferred to General of the Flying Dragon, garrison commander of Yongcheng" through "all the Di were shaken in awe" belong under "eight years in office."

sentences.zh: 這裏「遷離城鎮將」五字則是衍文。

translations.literal: Here the five characters "transferred to Licheng garrison commander" are redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The five characters "transferred to Licheng garrison commander" are an interpolation.

sentences.zh: 原文當作：……朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The original text should read: …The court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The original text should read: "…The court praised him."

sentences.zh: 雍州人王叔保等三百人表乞藻為騃奴戍主。

translations.literal: Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao and others memorialized begging that Zao be made garrison commander of Yinu.
translations.idiomatic: "Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao asked that Zao be made garrison commander of Yinu."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「選曹已用人，藻有惠政，自宜他敍。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The selection office has already appointed someone; Zao has benevolent government and should receive another posting.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The selection office has already filled the post. Zao's benevolent rule deserves another appointment."

sentences.zh: 」在任八年，遷龍驤將軍、雍城鎮將。

translations.literal: " After eight years in office he was transferred to General of the Flying Dragon and garrison commander of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: "After eight years in office he was made General of the Flying Dragon and garrison commander of Yongcheng."

sentences.zh: 先是氐豪徐成、楊黑等驅逐鎮將，故以藻代之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Di chieftains Xu Cheng and Yang Hei and others had driven off the garrison commander, and therefore Zao was sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Di chieftains Xu Cheng and Yang Hei had expelled the garrison commander, and Zao was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，擒獲成、黑等，斬之以徇，羣氐震慴。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison he captured Cheng, Hei, and the others and beheaded them as a warning; all the Di were shaken in awe.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he captured Cheng, Hei, and their fellows, executed them as a warning, and all the Di were cowed.

sentences.zh: 太和中，改鎮為岐州，以藻為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the garrison was changed to Qi Province and Zao was made Governor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era the garrison became Qi Province and Zao was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 詣長安拜文明太后父燕宣王廟 諸本「廟」下有「令」字，北史卷四五傅永傳無。

translations.literal: He went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of the civilized empress's father, Prince Yan of Xu—various editions have the character ling after miao; the Beishi juan 45 biography of Fu Yong does not.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "He went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of the civilized empress's father, Prince Yan of Xu"—some editions add ling after "temple"; the Beishi biography of Fu Yong, juan 45, does not.

sentences.zh: 按拜燕宣王廟加官賜爵屢見卷五六鄭羲傳，卷七二陽尼附陽藻傳、李叔虎附李述傳、卷八九酷吏高遵傳。

translations.literal: According to worship at Prince Yan of Xu's temple with added office and enfeoffment, this is seen repeatedly in juan 56 biography of Zheng Yi, juan 72 Yang Ni with appended biography of Yang Zao, Li Shuhu with appended biography of Li Shu, and juan 89 cruel officials biography of Gao Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Grants of office and noble rank for worship at Prince Yan of Xu's temple appear often in the biographies of Zheng Yi (juan 56), Yang Zao (juan 72), Li Shu (juan 72), and Gao Zun (juan 89).

sentences.zh: 若授廟令，則廟本在長安，不必贅言「詣長安」，且廟令卑官，史例也不稱「拜」。

translations.literal: If he were granted temple director, the temple was originally in Chang'an and there was no need to add "went to Chang'an," and moreover temple director was a low office and historiographic precedent does not call it "worship.
translations.idiomatic: If the text meant temple director, the temple was already in Chang'an and the journey would be redundant; moreover a temple directorship was a minor post and histories do not style it "worship."

sentences.zh: 「令」字衍，今據刪。

translations.literal: The character ling is redundant; it is deleted on this authority.
translations.idiomatic: The character ling is an interpolation and is deleted here.

sentences.zh: 肅復令永討之 諸本「永」訛「大」，今據北史卷四五、冊府卷三六四

translations.literal: Su again ordered Yong to attack him—various editions corrupt yong as da; now according to Beishi juan 45 and Cefu juan 364
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "Su again ordered Yong to attack him"—editions corrupt Yong as Da; the reading Yong is restored from the Beishi, juan 45, and Cefu, juan 364,

translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "At dawn Shuye and the others arrived and encamped east of the city"—editions read dun ("encamp") as jiang ("river").

translations.idiomatic: has no jiang.

sentences.zh: 按戰事在豫州，今河南汝南一帶，楚王戍不得旁長江，「江」字乃「頓」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: According to the fact that the fighting was in Yuzhou, in present-day Henan Runan region, the Prince of Chu's garrison could not lie beside the Yangzi; the character jiang is a corruption of dun and is corrected on this authority.
translations.idiomatic: The battle was in Yuzhou, in modern Henan around Runan; the Prince of Chu's camp could not have stood on the Yangzi. Jiang is a corruption of dun and is corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其信武將軍衡州刺史張齊因民心之怨 按張齊，梁書卷一七有傳，從未為衡州刺史，梁之衡州也不在此，疑有誤。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Hengzhou Zhang Qi because of the people's resentment—according to Zhang Qi, the Liangshu juan 17 has a biography; he was never Governor of Hengzhou, and Liang's Hengzhou was also not in this place; there is probably error.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "Xiao Yan sent his Trustworthy Martial General and Governor of Hengzhou Zhang Qi because of popular resentment"—the Liangshu, juan 17, biographies Zhang Qi but never as Governor of Hengzhou, and Liang's Hengzhou was not in this region. The title is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 參卷九校記[一]。

translations.literal: See collation note [1] to juan 9.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note [1] to juan 9.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史王太洪等十餘將所在拒塞 按下文說「斬太洪」，自即此「王太洪」。

translations.literal: Governor of Liangzhou Wang Taihong and more than ten generals everywhere blocked and obstructed—according to the text below saying "beheaded Taihong," this is naturally this "Wang Taihong."
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "Governor of Liangzhou Wang Taihong and more than ten generals blocked the way"—below the text says Taihong was beheaded, so this should be the same man.

sentences.zh: 然卷九肅宗紀熙平元年五月及卷九八蕭衍傳都作「斬其將任太洪」。

translations.literal: Yet the annals in juan 9, Emperor Xiaozong's reign, first year of Xiping, fifth month, and juan 98 biography of Xiao Yan all read "beheaded his general Ren Taihong."
translations.idiomatic: Yet juan 9 of the annals (Xiping year 1, month 5) and juan 98 (biography of Xiao Yan) both read "beheaded the general Ren Taihong."

sentences.zh: 紀於上年

translations.literal: The annals of the previous year
translations.idiomatic: The annals of the previous year

sentences.zh: 〈景明四年〉

translations.literal: 〈Jingming year 4〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Jingming year 4〉

sentences.zh: 二月稱「蕭衍寧州刺史任太洪率眾寇關城」，卷九八同，應即此被斬之梁將。

translations.literal: in the second month say "Xiao Yan's Governor of Ningzhou Ren Taihong led a host to raid Guancheng"; juan 98 agrees; this should be the Liang general beheaded here.
translations.idiomatic: in month 2 record, "Xiao Yan's Governor of Ningzhou Ren Taihong led troops against Guancheng"; juan 98 agrees. That is presumably the officer beheaded here.

sentences.zh: 這裏「王」字乃「任」字之訛。

translations.literal: Here the character wang is a corruption for ren.
translations.idiomatic: Here Wang is a corruption of Ren.

sentences.zh: 乾愛子三寶與房法壽等同効盤陽 諸本「効」下旁注「疑」字。

translations.literal: Qian'ai's son Sanbao, together with Fang Fashou and others, together rendered merit at Panyang—various editions have the character yi of "doubt" as a side note below xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note: "Qian'ai's son Sanbao, with Fang Fashou and others, won merit at Panyang"—editions carry a side note "doubt" after xiao ("render merit").

sentences.zh: 按房法壽襲取盤陽以降魏，事見卷四三本傳，「同効盤陽」意謂同在盤陽立功。

translations.literal: According to Fang Fashou's seizure of Panyang to submit to Wei, seen in juan 43 of this book, his biography, "together rendering merit at Panyang" means together winning merit at Panyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Fashou's seizure of Panyang for Wei appears in juan 43. "Together rendering merit at Panyang" means they won merit there together.

sentences.zh: 並無可疑，今刪旁注。

translations.literal: There is nothing doubtful; the side note is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing is doubtful; the side note is deleted.
